sources.text: The published 93-layer text decoder uses 69 KDA and 24 gated NoPE MLA layers, eight depth archives, and one initial dense SiTU-GLU layer. Each subsequent MoE has 896 routed experts, 16 selected per token and two shared experts.

BF16 analytical model with FP32 KDA matrix state, BF16 short-convolution history, and an absorbed MLA cache. NoPE passes both query/key channel sets unchanged. Attention Residual archives contain current-call token activations across depth; they do not persist as KV across Decode calls.

Attention and expert compute uses a logical materialized reference, explicit arithmetic proxies and an upper bound on distinct selected routed expert weights. The released MXFP4 storage and fused kernels, chunk KDA kernel execution, and vision encoder are outside this BF16 profile.

Use local batch, heads, route slots, expert count and intermediate width from the declared layouts. Attention Residual archives are activations for the active request lanes. Link costs use the declared ring model.

Shard KDA and Gated MLA projections by head. Each KDA rank maintains its own FP32 matrix and BF16 convolution history. MLA latent and shared NoPE key caches are replicated. Reduce attention before each depth mixing or residual consumer.

Shard routed expert weights by contiguous ownership. Preserve the full per-token Top-K with balanced valid slots and padding to ceil(K/EP). Gather valid routes and reduce the BF16 latent result before its RMSNorm and up projection.

Shard paired gate and up features and matching down projection inputs within each routed expert. Reduce the BF16 latent result before RMSNorm. Router, latent input projections and shared experts are replicated across these ranks.
